title: INTERNET MULTIMEDIA BROADCASTING BUSINESS ACT
full_text:
CHAPTER 1 GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to protect users' rights and interests, develop related technologies and industries, protect the public interest in broadcasting, and enhance national culture, and thereby contribute to the development of the national economy and the promotion of public welfare, by ensuring the proper operation of broadcasting businesses using Internet multimedia and similar means in an environment of increasing convergence between broadcasting and telecommunications. <Amended 2020.6.9>

Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act are defined as follows. <Amended 2010.3.22, 2014.12.30, 2020.6.9>
1. "Internet multimedia broadcasting" means broadcasting that uses broadband integrated information and communications networks, etc. (whether owned or leased, but excluding telecommunications line facilities used for services using frequencies allocated for operating a facilities-based telecommunications business under Article 10 (1) 1 of the Radio Waves Act), through an interactive Internet protocol method with a certain quality of service assured, to provide users, through television receivers and similar devices, with a combination of content such as data, images, voice, sound, and electronic commerce, including real-time broadcast programs.
2. "Broadband integrated information and communications networks, etc." means hyper-connected intelligent information and communications networks under subparagraph 9 of Article 2 of the Framework Act on Intelligent Informatization and telecommunications line facilities under subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Telecommunications Business Act.
3. "Real-time broadcast programs" means broadcast programs scheduled and transmitted or provided by an Internet multimedia broadcasting content provider or a broadcasting business entity under subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Broadcasting Act, which are provided simultaneously without any change to their content or scheduling.
4. "Internet multimedia broadcasting business" means either of the following businesses:
(a) Internet multimedia broadcasting service business: A business in which an Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider that has been supplied with content pursuant to Article 18 (1) for provision through Internet multimedia broadcasting provides that content to users;
(b) Internet multimedia broadcasting content business: A business supplying Internet multimedia content to Internet multimedia broadcasting service providers.
5. "Internet multimedia broadcasting business entity" means either of the following business entities:
(a) Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider: A person who has obtained permission under Article 4 (1) to operate an Internet multimedia broadcasting service business;
(b) Internet multimedia broadcasting content provider: A person who has filed a report, registered, or obtained approval under Article 18 (2) to operate an Internet multimedia broadcasting content business.

Article 3 (Relationship to Other Acts) This Act shall apply to Internet multimedia broadcasting businesses in preference to other Acts.

CHAPTER 2 PERMISSION FOR BUSINESS

Article 4 (Permission for Internet Multimedia Broadcasting Service Business)
① A person who intends to operate an Internet multimedia broadcasting service business shall obtain permission from the Korea Media and Communications Commission. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>
② Only a corporation may be granted permission under paragraph ①. <Amended 2020.6.9>
③ A person who intends to obtain permission under paragraph ① shall submit an application for permission containing the following matters to the Korea Media and Communications Commission. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>
1. The name and address of the corporation and the name of its representative;
2. A business plan, including a content procurement plan;
3. Documents demonstrating financial and technical capabilities;
4. A facilities plan (including a leasing plan where major facilities are to be leased);
5. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree.
④ When granting permission for an Internet multimedia broadcasting service business, the Korea Media and Communications Commission shall examine the following matters and publicly announce the results. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2020.6.9, 2025.10.1>
1. The feasibility of fulfilling the public responsibility, fairness, and public interest of broadcasting;
2. The appropriateness of the content procurement plan and its contribution to the development of the broadcast video industry;
3. The adequacy of the plan to secure fair competition in the pay broadcasting market;
4. The adequacy of the management plan, including organization and personnel management;
5. Financial and technical capabilities;
6. Where the applicant is a corporation in the process of incorporation, whether its incorporation is certain;
7. Whether the facilities plan is adequate;
8. Other matters necessary for conducting the business.
⑤ Deleted. <2008.2.29>
⑥ When granting permission, the Korea Media and Communications Commission shall do so within 3 months unless there is a particular ground for disqualification. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2020.6.9, 2025.10.1>
⑦ The procedures necessary for permission for an Internet multimedia broadcasting service business under paragraph ①, the allocation of points to examination criteria, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2008.2.29>

Article 5 (Term of Validity of Permission) The term of validity of permission for an Internet multimedia broadcasting service business under Article 4 (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree within a maximum of 7 years. <Amended 2014.12.30>

Article 5-2 (Renewal of Permission)
① An Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider that intends to continue operating its Internet multimedia broadcasting service business after the expiry of its permission shall obtain renewed permission from the Korea Media and Communications Commission. <Amended 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>
② When renewing permission under paragraph ①, the Korea Media and Communications Commission shall examine the matters specified in each subparagraph of Article 4 (4) and the following matters, and publicly announce the results. <Amended 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>
1. Whether the business plan, conditions of permission, and other requirements applicable at the time of the previous permission have been fulfilled;
2. The substance and number of corrective orders and dispositions imposing penalty surcharges or administrative fines issued by the Korea Media and Communications Commission, and whether they have been complied with.
③ Article 4 (2), (3), (6), and (7) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the renewal of permission under paragraph ①.
④ Notwithstanding paragraph ①, if renewal under that paragraph has not been completed within the term of validity of the previous permission for reasons not attributable to the applicant for renewal, the previous permission shall be deemed valid until a decision is made on whether to renew it. <Added 2026.5.19>

Article 6 (Business Area)
① The entire country shall constitute a single business area for an Internet multimedia broadcasting service business. However, this shall not apply where, at the time permission for the business is granted under Article 4 (1), a small or medium enterprise under Article 2 (1) of the Framework Act on Small and Medium Enterprises requests otherwise and the Korea Media and Communications Commission finds a particular need. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>
② Where a facilities-based telecommunications business entity under Article 39 (3) 1 or 2 of the Telecommunications Business Act obtains permission under Article 4 (1), it shall commence services in all broadcasting areas publicly notified by the Korea Media and Communications Commission under Article 12 (2) of the Broadcasting Act within the period prescribed by Presidential Decree from the date permission is granted. However, if services cannot commence within the period specified in the main clause owing to a natural disaster or another unavoidable cause, the Korea Media and Communications Commission may extend that period once only, within the period prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2009.5.21, 2010.3.22, 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2020.6.9, 2025.10.1>

Article 7 (Grounds for Disqualification)
① None of the following persons may operate an Internet multimedia broadcasting service business under Article 4 (1). <Amended 2020.6.9>
1. The State or a local government;
2. A corporation exceeding the restrictions on ownership of stocks or shares under Articles 8 and 9;
3. A person for whom 3 years have not elapsed since permission was revoked under Article 24 (1).
② None of the following persons may be an executive officer of a corporation granted permission under Article 4 (1). <Amended 2014.6.3, 2020.6.9>
1. A minor or a person under adult guardianship;
2. Deleted. <2015.12.22>
3. A person sentenced to a fine or a heavier punishment for violating this Act, the Broadcasting Act, the Framework Act on Telecommunications, the Telecommunications Business Act, or the Act on Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilization and Information Protection, Etc., for whom 3 years have not elapsed since completion of execution of the sentence (including cases deemed to constitute completion of its execution) or exemption from its execution;
4. A person sentenced to imprisonment without labor or a heavier custodial sentence for an offense under Articles 87 through 90, 92, or 101 of the Criminal Act, Articles 5 through 8, 9 (2), or 11 through 16 of the Military Criminal Act, or Articles 3 through 9 of the National Security Act, whose sentence has not finished being executed or for whom it has not been finally determined that the sentence will not be executed, or who is within a period of suspension of execution of the sentence;
5. A person subject to the execution of a security surveillance disposition under the Security Surveillance Act or medical treatment and custody under the Medical Treatment and Custody Act.
③ None of the following persons may be the representative of a corporation granted permission under Article 4 (1). <Amended 2015.12.22>
1. A foreigner or a representative of a foreign corporation or organization;
2. A person declared bankrupt who has not been reinstated.

Article 8 (Prohibition of Concurrent Operation)
① Where an Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider issues stocks, they shall be registered stocks.
② A corporation operating a newspaper under the Act on the Promotion of Newspapers, Etc. or a news agency under the News Agency Promotion Act (including specially related persons prescribed by Presidential Decree) shall not own more than 49 percent of the total stocks or shares of an Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider. <Amended 2009.7.31>
③ A company belonging to a business group which falls within the criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as total assets, among the business groups under subparagraph 11 of Article 2 of the Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Act, and its affiliates (including specially related persons prescribed by Presidential Decree), or a corporation operating a newspaper under the Act on the Promotion of Newspapers, Etc. or a news agency under the News Agency Promotion Act (including specially related persons prescribed by Presidential Decree), shall not own more than 49 percent of the total stocks or shares of an Internet multimedia broadcasting content provider that provides general programming or programming specializing in news. <Amended 2009.7.31, 2020.12.29>
④ Deleted. <2024.10.22>

Article 9 (Restrictions on Foreign Ownership of Stocks)
① A person falling under any of the following subparagraphs shall not, in combination with persons falling under any of the other subparagraphs, own stocks (limited to voting stocks and including equivalents of voting stocks, such as stock depositary receipts, and equity interests; hereinafter the same shall apply) or shares exceeding 49 percent of the total issued stocks or shares of an Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider. <Amended 2014.12.30, 2020.6.9>
1. A foreign government or organization;
2. A foreigner;
3. A corporation whose largest shareholder is a foreign government or organization or a foreigner (including specially related persons under Article 9 (1) 1 of the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act; hereinafter the same shall apply in this subparagraph and paragraph ② 3), and in which that foreign government or organization or foreigner owns at least 15 percent of the total issued stocks (excluding a corporation owning less than 1 percent of the total issued stocks or shares of the relevant Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider).
② A person falling under any of the following subparagraphs shall not, in combination with persons falling under any of the other subparagraphs, own stocks or shares exceeding 49 percent of the total issued stocks or shares of an Internet multimedia broadcasting content provider (excluding a provider of general programming or programming specializing in news). However, in the case of an Internet multimedia broadcasting content provider (excluding a provider of general programming, programming specializing in news, or programming specializing in product presentations and sales), a corporation in which stocks or shares are owned by a government or organization of, or a foreigner from, a country that is a party to a free trade agreement designated and publicly notified by the Korea Media and Communications Commission among the bilateral or multilateral free trade agreements concluded by the Republic of Korea with foreign countries and in force shall not be regarded as a person falling under subparagraph 3, even if it meets the requirements of that subparagraph. <Added 2014.12.30, 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>
1. A foreign government or organization;
2. A foreigner;
3. A corporation in which the aggregate stocks or shares owned by foreign governments or organizations or foreigners exceed 50 percent of its total stocks or shares (including a case in which a foreign government or organization or a foreigner is the largest equity contributor).
③ A person falling under any subparagraph of paragraph ② shall not own more than 20 percent of the total stocks or shares of an Internet multimedia broadcasting content provider that provides general programming or programming specializing in news. <Amended 2009.7.31, 2014.12.30>

Article 10 (Restrictions on Shareholders with Excess Holdings)
① In the event of a violation of Article 8 or 9, a person owning the stocks or shares that caused the violation shall not exercise voting rights in respect of those holdings or the excess portion thereof.
② The Korea Media and Communications Commission may order a person who has violated Article 8 or 9, or an owner of the stocks or shares that caused the violation, to rectify the relevant matter within a specified period not exceeding 6 months. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>
③ A person ordered to take corrective measures under paragraph ② shall rectify the relevant matter within that period.

Article 11 (Permission for Changes)
① A person granted permission for an Internet multimedia broadcasting service business under Article 4 (1) shall obtain permission for a change where the person intends to change any of the following matters covered by the permission. <Amended 2014.6.3, 2024.1.23, 2025.10.1>
1. A merger or division of an Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider. However, where the person intends to merge with a corporation that is an affiliate under subparagraph 12 of Article 2 of the Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Act, the person shall file a report with the Korea Media and Communications Commission as prescribed by Presidential Decree;
2. Transfer of all or part of an Internet multimedia broadcasting service business. In such a case, the transferee of the business shall also obtain permission for an Internet multimedia broadcasting service business under Article 4;
3. A change in the business area.
② Article 4 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the procedures for permission for changes, the matters to be examined, and related matters.
③ A person granted permission for an Internet multimedia broadcasting service business under Article 4 (1) shall report to the Korea Media and Communications Commission without delay upon changing any of the following matters. <Added 2014.6.3, 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>
1. The representative;
2. The person responsible for broadcast programming;
3. The corporate or trade name;
4. The location of the principal office.
④ Upon receiving a report under the proviso of paragraph ① 1, the Korea Media and Communications Commission shall examine its contents and accept the report if it meets the criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree, including the truthfulness of the reported contents. In such a case, details such as the procedures for acceptance shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added 2024.1.23, 2025.10.1>

CHAPTER 3 GUARANTEE AND PROMOTION OF FAIR COMPETITION

Article 12 (Promotion of Fair Competition)
① The Government shall endeavor to establish an efficient competitive system and create an environment of fair competition for Internet multimedia broadcasting service businesses, and shall ensure that market power in other businesses is not improperly transferred to Internet multimedia broadcasting service businesses.
② Competition in Internet multimedia broadcasting service businesses shall be assessed in order to formulate competition policies for establishing an efficient competitive system and creating an environment of fair competition under paragraph ①. <Amended 2011.7.14>
③ The assessment of competition under paragraph ② shall be conducted by the Broadcasting Market Competition Assessment Committee under Article 35-5 (1) of the Broadcasting Act. <Amended 2011.7.14>
④ Specific methods and other matters for preventing market power in other businesses from being improperly transferred to Internet multimedia broadcasting service businesses shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2011.7.14>
⑤ Deleted. <2011.7.14>

Article 13 (Restrictions on Market Share)
① An individual Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider, together with the following broadcasting business entities specially related to it, shall not provide services to more than 1/3 of the total subscribers to pay broadcasting businesses, including Internet multimedia broadcasting, cable television broadcasting, and satellite broadcasting. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2015.3.27>
1. Internet multimedia broadcasting service providers;
2. Cable television broadcasting business entities under subparagraph 3 (b) of Article 2 of the Broadcasting Act;
3. Satellite broadcasting business entities under subparagraph 3 (c) of Article 2 of the Broadcasting Act.
② Where an Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider comes to violate paragraph ①, the Korea Media and Communications Commission may order the provider to rectify the relevant matter within a specified period not exceeding 6 months. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>
③ A provider ordered to take corrective measures under paragraph ② shall rectify the relevant matter within that period.
④ The Korea Media and Communications Commission may designate areas such as islands and mountainous areas where only satellite broadcasting can be received as exceptional areas that may be excluded when calculating the number of subscribers under paragraph ①. <Added 2015.3.27, 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>
⑤ Matters necessary for calculating and verifying the number of subscribers under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added 2015.3.27>

Article 14 (Equal Provision of Telecommunications Facilities)
① Where a person intending to operate an Internet multimedia broadcasting service business requests access to and use of telecommunications facilities essential to providing the relevant service, an Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider shall not refuse the request without a reasonable and justifiable ground, such as insufficient capacity in its own facilities or the protection of trade secrets.
② An Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider shall not discontinue or restrict the use of its own facilities being used by another Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider without a reasonable and justifiable ground.
③ An Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider shall not provide its own facilities to another Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider at unjustifiably discriminatory prices or on unjustifiably discriminatory terms.
④ Necessary matters concerning the scope of telecommunications facilities under paragraphs ① through ③, grounds for refusing, discontinuing, or restricting the provision of facilities, the methods and procedures for providing facilities, and principles for calculating charges for the use of facilities shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 14-2 (Public Notification of Technical Standards) The Korea Media and Communications Commission shall establish and publicly notify technical standards concerning the installation and maintenance of the broadcasting station facilities of Internet multimedia broadcasting service providers and concerning transmission facilities, line facilities, and similar facilities. <Amended 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>

Article 15 (Reporting of Terms and Conditions of Use)
① An Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider shall establish terms and conditions concerning charges and conditions for use of the services it intends to provide (hereinafter referred to as "terms and conditions of use") and report them to the Korea Media and Communications Commission. The same shall apply when the provider intends to change reported terms and conditions of use. <Amended 2025.10.1>
② Terms and conditions of use shall meet all of the following requirements:
1. Charges for use shall be clearly specified;
2. They shall contain no provision violating Article 17 (1) 4 or 6.
③ Notwithstanding paragraph ①, where charges fall under any of the following subparagraphs, the relevant terms and conditions of use shall be approved by the Korea Media and Communications Commission. The same shall apply when approved terms and conditions of use are to be changed. <Amended 2025.10.1>
1. Charges for the minimum-channel package specified in the terms and conditions of use (meaning the lowest-priced package among pay broadcasting packages for which payment is charged for a bundle of multiple channels; hereinafter the same shall apply);
2. Charges for a package bundling Internet multimedia broadcasting with services providing facilities-based telecommunications services under subparagraph 11 of Article 2 of the Telecommunications Business Act.
④ A person seeking approval or approval of a change to terms and conditions of use under paragraph ③ shall submit to the Korea Media and Communications Commission the supporting data for calculating charges, including subscription fees, basic fees, usage fees, additional service fees, and actual expenses (including a comparison of the old and new provisions in the case of a change). <Amended 2025.10.1>
⑤ When intending to grant approval or approval of a change to terms and conditions of use under paragraph ③, the Korea Media and Communications Commission shall consider whether the following criteria are met. <Amended 2025.10.1>
1. The minimum-channel package specified in the terms and conditions of use shall not be disproportionately concentrated on a particular field of broadcasting;
2. Charges for use shall have been reasonably calculated, taking into account supply costs, revenue, cost savings attributable to the method of providing the service, the impact on an environment of fair competition, and similar factors.
⑥ Details concerning the procedures for reporting, reporting changes, approval, and approval of changes under paragraphs ① through ⑤ shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 16 (Protection of Users)
① An Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider shall promptly address justified opinions or complaints raised by users concerning the services it provides.
② An Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider shall take measures to protect information concerning individual users obtained in the course of providing services or telecommunications facilities, and shall not disclose personal information so obtained. However, this shall not apply where the data subject consents or where disclosure follows a lawful procedure under another Act.
③ An Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider that causes damage to a user through the improper provision of information concerning an individual user under paragraph ② shall provide appropriate compensation.

Article 16-2 (Assessment of the Quality of Internet Multimedia Broadcasting Services)
① The Korea Media and Communications Commission may assess the quality of services provided by Internet multimedia broadcasting business entities (hereinafter referred to as "service quality") in order to improve the quality of Internet multimedia broadcasting services and enhance benefits to viewers. <Amended 2025.10.1>
② The Korea Media and Communications Commission may request Internet multimedia broadcasting business entities to submit data necessary for the assessment of service quality under paragraph ①. A business entity receiving such a request shall comply unless there is a special reason not to do so. <Amended 2025.10.1>
③ Where the Korea Media and Communications Commission assesses service quality under paragraph ①, it shall disclose the results. <Amended 2025.10.1>
④ Details concerning the assessment of service quality under paragraph ①, the methods and procedures for submitting data under paragraph ②, and disclosure of service quality assessment results under paragraph ③ shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 16-3 (Provision of Korean Sign Language, Closed Captions, and Audio Description)
① Where an Internet multimedia broadcasting business entity produces content itself for the services it provides, it shall provide Korean Sign Language, closed captions, audio description, and similar assistance to facilitate use by persons with disabilities.
② The Government may subsidize the expenses necessary for Internet multimedia broadcasting business entities to provide Korean Sign Language, closed captions, audio description, and similar assistance under paragraph ①.

Article 17 (Prohibited Acts)
① An Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider shall neither engage in any of the following acts that undermine or are likely to undermine fair competition among business entities or users' interests nor cause a third party to engage in such an act:
1. Refusing to provide Internet multimedia broadcasting services without a justifiable ground;
2. Providing Internet multimedia broadcasting services on terms different from the terms and conditions of use, or charging fees on terms different from the contract for use;
3. Improperly appropriating user information learned in the course of providing Internet multimedia broadcasting services;
4. Providing Internet multimedia broadcasting services at substantially advantageous or disadvantageous charges or on substantially advantageous or disadvantageous conditions through unjustified discrimination among users;
5. Using a position of superiority to compel an Internet multimedia broadcasting content provider to enter into an unfair contract or refusing an appropriate distribution of revenue;
6. Unjustifiably interfering with the viewing of another broadcasting business entity's broadcasts or with the conclusion of a service provision contract;
7. Refusing, discontinuing, or restricting, without a justifiable ground, the use of or access to telecommunications facilities such as utility poles, conduits, and telecommunications ducts essential to the provision of services by another broadcasting business entity.
② Where an Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider commits an act falling under any subparagraph of paragraph ①, the Korea Media and Communications Commission may, in consultation with the Fair Trade Commission, impose on that provider a penalty surcharge prescribed by Presidential Decree not exceeding 2 percent of its sales, taking into account the nature and seriousness of the violation, its duration and frequency, the amount of profit obtained through it, and similar matters. However, in cases prescribed by Presidential Decree where there are no sales or it is difficult to calculate sales, a penalty surcharge not exceeding 500 million won may be imposed. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2025.10.1>
③ If a person subject to a disposition imposing a penalty surcharge under paragraph ② fails to pay it by the payment deadline, the Korea Media and Communications Commission shall collect it in accordance with the procedure for collecting delinquent national taxes. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2020.6.9, 2025.10.1>
④ Matters necessary concerning detailed types and criteria for the acts specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER 4 INTERNET MULTIMEDIA BROADCASTING CONTENT

Article 18 (Supply of Content)
① Any broadcasting business entity under subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Broadcasting Act, value-added telecommunications business entity under Article 22 of the Telecommunications Business Act, person engaged in producing or supplying content under another Act, or other person producing or supplying content may supply content for Internet multimedia broadcasting to an Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider. <Amended 2010.3.22, 2014.6.3>
② A person intending to supply content under paragraph ① shall file a report with or register with the Korea Media and Communications Commission. However, a person intending to provide an Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider with content specializing in news, content offering general programming across various fields such as news, culture, and entertainment, or content specializing in product presentations and sales shall obtain approval from the Korea Media and Communications Commission. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>
③ The following persons shall be deemed to have filed a report, registered, or obtained approval under paragraph ②. <Added 2014.6.3>
1. A broadcasting business entity under subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Broadcasting Act (in the case of a cable television broadcasting business entity or satellite broadcasting business entity, limited to content supplied through a channel it uses directly);
2. A value-added telecommunications business entity under Article 22 of the Telecommunications Business Act.
④ Matters concerning the specific procedures and methods necessary for reporting, registration, and approval under paragraph ② shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2014.6.3>

Article 18-2 (Requirements for Registration) Article 9-2 of the Broadcasting Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the requirements for registration of a person intending to register as an Internet multimedia broadcasting content provider under the main clause of Article 18 (2). In such a case, "program-providing business" shall be construed as "Internet multimedia broadcasting content business".

Article 19 (Measures for Development of Content Businesses) Except as otherwise expressly provided in another Act, the Government shall separately establish and implement measures to develop content businesses, including securing the financial resources necessary to promote fair competition among content supplied to Internet multimedia broadcasting service providers and to foster the related industries.

Article 20 (Equal Access to Content)
① Where the Korea Media and Communications Commission publicly notifies, according to criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree, a broadcast program provided by an Internet multimedia broadcasting content provider that has filed a report, registered, or obtained approval under Article 18 (2) (hereinafter referred to as a "major broadcast program"), the content provider shall also provide that program without discrimination to other Internet multimedia broadcasting service providers at a fair and reasonable price so that the general public can view it, and shall not undermine viewers' interests or the order of fair trade in contracting for major broadcast programs or similar dealings. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2020.6.9, 2025.10.1>
② When publicly notifying major broadcast programs under paragraph ①, the Korea Media and Communications Commission shall hear the opinions of the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism, broadcasting business entities, and viewers. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2020.6.9, 2025.10.1>
③ The Korea Media and Communications Commission may order an Internet multimedia broadcasting content provider that violates paragraph ① to take necessary corrective measures, including cessation of the prohibited act. Before ordering corrective measures, the Commission shall specify a period and give the party an opportunity to state its views. However, this shall not apply where the party fails to respond without a justifiable ground. <Amended 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>

Article 21 (Composition and Operation of Broadcast Programs)
① An Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider shall not operate a channel for its own direct use.
② Articles 32, 33, and 100 of the Broadcasting Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the review of the content of real-time broadcast programs provided by Internet multimedia broadcasting content providers.
③ Article 70 (1) through (3) and (8) of the Broadcasting Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to real-time broadcast programs provided by Internet multimedia broadcasting service providers. In such a case, "cable television broadcasting business entity" shall be construed as "Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider", and "channel" as "a unit of real-time broadcast programs provided by an Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider". <Amended 2014.12.30>
④ Articles 69, 71 through 74, 76, 76-3, 76-5, 78 (1) through (4), 78-2, and 83 of the Broadcasting Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to content providers' scheduling of programs, scheduling of domestic broadcast programs, scheduling of externally produced broadcast programs, advertising, sponsorship announcements, supply of programs, measures to guarantee universal viewing rights, recommendations on sequential scheduling of relay broadcasts, retransmission, and recording and preservation of broadcast content. In such a case, "broadcasting business entity" shall be construed as "Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider or Internet multimedia broadcasting content provider". <Amended 2014.12.30>
⑤ Results of broadcasting under Article 83 (1) of the Broadcasting Act, as applied mutatis mutandis under the former part of paragraph ④, shall be submitted to the Korea Media and Communications Commission. <Added 2014.12.30, 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>
⑥ Article 40 of the Framework Act on Broadcasting Communications Development shall apply mutatis mutandis to disaster broadcasting. <Amended 2013.3.23, 2014.12.30>

CHAPTER 5 SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 22 (Temporary Suspension or Closure of Business)
① Where an Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider intends to temporarily suspend or close all or part of its business, it shall notify users of the relevant service and report the details to the Korea Media and Communications Commission no later than 30 days before the scheduled date of suspension or closure. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2020.6.9, 2025.10.1>
② Where an Internet multimedia broadcasting content provider intends to temporarily suspend or close all or part of its business, it shall report the details to the Korea Media and Communications Commission. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2020.6.9, 2025.10.1>

Article 23 Deleted. <2010.3.22>

Article 24 (Revocation of Permission and Suspension of Business)
① Where an Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the Korea Media and Communications Commission may revoke permission for the relevant business under this Act or order suspension of its business for a specified period not exceeding 1 year. However, where the provider falls under subparagraph 1, permission shall be revoked. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>
1. Where permission under Article 4 (1) was obtained by fraud or other improper means;
2. Where the business has not commenced within 1 year from the date permission under Article 4 (1) was granted, or has remained temporarily suspended for 1 year or longer;
3. Where an order under Article 10 (2) or 13 (2) has not been complied with.
② The criteria and procedures for dispositions under paragraph ① and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 24-2 (Hearings) Where the Korea Media and Communications Commission intends to revoke permission for an Internet multimedia broadcasting service business under Article 24 (1), it shall hold a hearing. <Amended 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>

Article 25 (Penalty Surcharges)
① Where an Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider falls under any subparagraph of Article 24 (1) and revocation of permission or suspension of business is likely to cause serious inconvenience to users of the business or others, or otherwise harm the public interest, the Korea Media and Communications Commission may, in lieu of suspending the business or revoking permission, impose a penalty surcharge not exceeding 3 percent of sales from the Internet multimedia broadcasting service business, taking into account the grounds for suspension or revocation, the amount of profit obtained from the violation, and similar matters. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2020.6.9, 2025.10.1>
② Where a person subject to a disposition imposing a penalty surcharge under paragraph ① fails to pay it by the payment deadline, the Korea Media and Communications Commission shall collect it in accordance with the procedure for collecting delinquent national taxes. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2020.6.9, 2025.10.1>
③ The types of violations subject to penalty surcharges under paragraph ①, the amounts of such surcharges, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 26 (Corrective Orders)
① Where an Internet multimedia broadcasting business entity falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the Korea Media and Communications Commission shall order it to take corrective measures. However, violations of Article 17 (1) are excluded. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2014.12.30, 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>
1. Where its business processing procedures are found to substantially undermine users' interests;
2. Where it fails promptly to take necessary measures when an accident or similar event disrupts the provision of Internet multimedia broadcasting;
3. Where it otherwise violates this Act or an order issued under this Act.
② The Korea Media and Communications Commission may order a person operating an Internet multimedia broadcasting service business without permission under Article 4 (1) to cease providing the relevant service. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>
③ The Korea Media and Communications Commission may order a person operating an Internet multimedia broadcasting content business without filing a report, registering, or obtaining approval under Article 18 (2) to cease providing the relevant service. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>
④ Where there is an act violating Article 17 (1), the Korea Media and Communications Commission may order the relevant business entity to take necessary corrective measures, including cessation of the violation, amendment of the terms and conditions of use, or deletion of contractual provisions. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2025.10.1>

Article 26-2 (Delegation and Entrustment of Authority) Part of the authority of the Korea Media and Communications Commission under this Act may be delegated to the heads of its subordinate agencies or entrusted to the heads of other administrative agencies or the heads of agencies subordinate to those administrative agencies, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>

Article 26-3 (Review of Regulations) The Korea Media and Communications Commission shall review the appropriateness of the submission of data for assessing service quality under Article 16-2 (2) by each date falling at 5-year intervals from January 1, 2021, and take necessary measures. <Amended 2025.10.1>

CHAPTER 6 PENAL PROVISIONS

Article 27 (Penalties)
① A person falling under any of the following subparagraphs shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than 2 years or a fine not exceeding 30 million won:
1. A person operating an Internet multimedia broadcasting service business without obtaining permission under Article 4 (1) (including permission for changes);
2. A person refusing a request for access to and use of essential telecommunications facilities without a reasonable and justifiable ground, in violation of Article 14 (1);
3. A person discontinuing or restricting, without a reasonable and justifiable ground, the use of its own facilities being used by another Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider, in violation of Article 14 (2);
4. A person providing its own facilities to another Internet multimedia broadcasting service provider at unjustifiably discriminatory prices or on unjustifiably discriminatory terms, in violation of Article 14 (3);
5. A person disclosing information in violation of Article 16 (2);
6. A person violating an order suspending business under Article 24 (1).
② Where a representative of a corporation, or an agent, employee, or other worker of a corporation or an individual, commits a violation under paragraph ① 2 through 4 in connection with the business of that corporation or individual, the corporation or individual shall also be subject to the fine prescribed in the relevant subparagraph, in addition to punishment of the offender. However, this shall not apply where the corporation or individual has not neglected due care and supervision concerning the relevant business to prevent the violation.

Article 28 (Administrative Fines)
① A person falling under any of the following subparagraphs shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 10 million won. <Amended 2022.1.11, 2024.1.23>
1. A person failing to file a report under the proviso of Article 11 (1) 1;
1-2. A person failing to submit data under Article 12 (4);
2. A person operating an Internet multimedia broadcasting service business without reporting terms and conditions of use or changes thereto, or without obtaining approval of such terms and conditions or changes thereto, in violation of Article 15 (1) or (3);
3. A person failing to submit data in violation of Article 15 (4);
4. A person failing to take measures to protect user information under Article 16 (2);
4-2. A person failing to submit necessary data without a special reason, in violation of Article 16-2 (2);
5. A person failing to file a report under Article 22;
6. A person failing to comply with a corrective order or similar measure under Article 26.
② Administrative fines under paragraph ① shall be imposed and collected by the Korea Media and Communications Commission as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>
